## Your own percentile {#find-your-own-percentile .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted in Task 4, in the workspace or in the browser lab: its output includes your **placement**
- The placement is the share of the `r fmt_n(nrow(spec_curve))` specifications on the curve with a more negative claim-aligned *r* than yours. For the reproduced specification it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(spec_curve$r_ca < curve_ref$r_ca))`
- The same statistic that places the reference results, computed for **you**
:::

::: {.fragment}
Paste your percentile in chat – hold – send on "go".
:::

::: notes
Your turn to be placed. Rerun try underscore spec with the choices that you submitted, in your workspace or in the browser lab, whichever you have open. The placement line in its output is the same statistic that places the reference results: the share of the eight hundred and sixty-four specifications on the curve that are more negative than yours. For the reproduced specification, my own model, it is sixty-seven per cent, so if you did not submit, that is your number. Two or three minutes. Then paste your percentile in chat, hold it, send on go. [go] Look at the range in the chat – the class spans a good stretch of the curve, and every one of you can now say where you stand relative to eight hundred and sixty-four justifiable alternatives. That sentence – "my estimate sits at the Nth percentile of the specification curve" – is a publishable way to report a robustness check, as long as you say how the curve was built.
:::
